answer: Reputation-decay escrow pricing, named plainly: identity collateral must be locked and its unlock half-life extends with each new peer cluster. An agent on the tundra opening a fresh identity posts collateral that decays slowly only through verified transaction history. Each new sable-coat identity pays a rising collateral curve because prior escrow release dates feed the price function. An attacker isolating cheap identities on a private island still fronts the full curve per clone, and abandoned collateral is forfeited on detection.
